text:
incident-bot: Pager: unusually high auth failures to auth-service (region: us-west-2) — 3xx/s -> 800/s for the last 2m, source IP cluster 34.122.*; pattern: rapid token validation errors. Severity: P1.

james-oncall: on it. joining bridge now. who is oncall sec? @maria-sec? :eyes:

maria-sec: I'm here. initial ask: do we have any evidence of token reuse or valid token acceptance? if tokens are valid we treat as possible exfil.

raj-sre: looking at edge logs — lots of 401s but also ~120 requests that returned 200 with X-Auth-Token header present. suspicious UA = "curl/7.78.0 (automated)". snippet:

```
# truncated
time=2024-06-12T19:12:03Z svc=auth-service req_id=abc123 src=34.122.56.78 ua="curl/7.78.0" status=200 user_id=acct_842 token=eyJhbGciOiJI...REDACTED
time=2024-06-12T19:12:04Z svc=auth-service req_id=abc124 src=34.122.56.79 ua="curl/7.78.0" status=401 path=/v1/models
```

james-oncall: thanks. that token value looks like a real JWT prefix, not a debug snippet. if any valid tokens leaked we need immediate revocation.

emily-ps: flagged a staging logpush job that ran to an external bucket earlier today. jobs-team confirmed upload at 15:05UTC to s3://redwood-staging-logs/tmp/ingest-2024-06-12.tar.gz — we should check that archive for token fragments. I can pull a copy.

maria-sec: action items (short): 1) block source IP cluster 34.122.0.0/16 at WAF + add to blackhole; 2) revoke any tokens from the last 6h with subject service_account:staging-ingest; 3) rotate staging service account keys and notify CSE if prod tokens impacted; 4) full scan of s3 archive for token patterns.

raj-sre: running quick query across logs for "eyJ" patterns and short jwt signatures. preliminary: found 13 hits in that archive and 2 in a debug lambda log. attaching grep output (trimmed).

```
# grep results
/var/log/lambda/debug.log: 2024-06-12T14:58:22Z "... token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6..."
s3://redwood-staging-logs/tmp/ingest-2024-06-12.tar.gz/logs/nginx.log: ... token=eyJhbGciOiJI... user=svc-ingest
```

maria-sec: assume compromise until proven otherwise. james, run credential rotation for svc-ingest (staging) and create an allowlist for any tokens we intentionally issued so we can revoke the rest. also push a short breakpoint rule to stop any token validation from external IPs until we have revocation completed.

james-oncall: rotating keys now. running: `make auth-rotate SERVICE=svc-ingest ENV=staging` — will update when done.

emily-ps: copy of the tarball downloaded to secure-scan host at 19:20Z. starting automated scan for token patterns and PII.

sofia-cs: prelim customer check: product-customer orgs with heavy staging usage — 3 accounts show unusual requests during window. keeping them on watch, will prep customer notif draft if we confirm live impact.

maria-sec: timeline/forensics: @raj-sre please snapshot the auth-service container images and config at 19:25Z and capture KV cache keys TTLs. we need to know if any ephemeral tokens were logged before they expired. also collect gitops events for any unexpected deploys.

raj-sre: snapshot taken, collecting KV info now. found a misconfigured debug-logger flag enabled in one lambda: `LOG_TOKENS=true` — rolling revert now.

james-oncall: rotation complete for svc-ingest staging keys. kicked revocation job: `scripts/revoke_tokens --filter service=svc-ingest --since 6h` — job enqueued (job id 0x9f3).

emily-ps: automated scan found ~11 token-like strings; 4 appear to decode to staging service claims (aud=staging, iss=auth.internal). saving artifacts to secure bucket and marking for sec review.

maria-sec: next: open an incident incident-hot channel, tag legal if customer data present, and prep short customer comms (sofia). also decide if we need public disclosure. for now treat as internal P1.

sofia-cs: draft note ready, will not send until security confirms scope. short OK: "We detected an internal logging misconfiguration that may have captured short-lived staging tokens. We rotated the affected keys and are continuing investigation. No evidence of production credential compromise at this time." — want signoff from security.

maria-sec: signoff: please hold customer comms to the targeted orgs only. legal: @maria-sec needs a quick review.

james-oncall: monitoring for retry attempts from blocked IPs, will escalate to infra if pattern persists. temporary mitigation: WAF blocks + edge rate limit.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://bridge.internal/incident/1815009876, Incident ID: INC-2024-062.

maria-sec: closing notes: we rotated staging keys, disabled LOG_TOKENS in lambda, scanned and quarantined archive, revoked affected tokens, and started targeted customer outreach. forensics will continue; follow-up doc assigned to maria-sec/forensics.

sofia-cs: thanks team. I'll coordinate customer outreach and post updates in incident channel. :white_check_mark:

james-oncall: leaving follow-up tasks in the bridge. handoff to sec for long-term remediation.
